paper.title_en: Phase-resolved spin-orbit exciton transfer with dressed quantum encodings
paper.abstract_en: A quantum simulation of a material runs on a register much smaller than the electronic problem behind it, and the map between the two decides what a measured correlation means. We study this map for spin--orbit exciton transfer across an Ir--Ir bond of a LiIrF$_6$-derived model. Exact references show that a bare product-state encoding has an amplitude floor above a 0.02 state tolerance at sampled times, whereas a polar-dressed encoding lowers the ten-window projected error from 0.320 to $3.54\times10^{-4}$. Three-CZ axial and two-CZ transverse circuits, run on IBM Kingston in eight acquisitions with 1.6 million shots, resolve population transfer together with both quadratures of the intersite coherence. Raw half-transfer Bell-projector scores reach 0.935 in two independent acquisitions, and on a second bond a coherent arm with lower bound 0.871 is separated from a matched dephased control. Across 2,520 model points, adaptive spectral encodings meet fixed accuracy targets with explicit dimension costs.
